NACA 63-815 safe-angle tool

Neural-network surrogate of 448 OpenFOAM k–ω SST simulations (Re 0.5–8 million), combined with the exact cavitation number. Enter an operating point to get the coefficients, the cavitation verdict and the largest safe angle of attack.

Illustration, not CFD. Ideal (potential) flow around a similar cambered foil, from the Joukowski conformal mapping with the Kutta condition; the circulation is set so the lift equals the surrogate's CL. Colours: that ideal-flow pressure, scaled so the suction peak equals the predicted Cp,min (light blue = suction peak, red = stagnation). White streaks: particles carried by the ideal flow. Orange: separated region after stall onset, drawn from how far the lift falls below its linear trend, not computed. White bubbles: a symbol drawn near the suction peak when σ < σi (more bubbles the further below). Our RANS model is single-phase and does not simulate bubbles; it predicts where the pressure falls to vapour pressure (cavitation inception). Press OpenFOAM field to see a computed flow field.

Pressure distribution: where cavitation starts

Section curves at this Reynolds number

How the numbers are made. Stage 1: a mean of five neural networks (2 hidden layers × 32 tanh neurons) gives CL, CD, Cm and σi = −Cp,min from (α, Re). Stall onset is the angle where lift falls 5 % below its linear trend. Stage 2: σ = (patm + ρgh − pv) / ½ρU², with U = Re ν / c for sea water at 15 °C (ITTC: ν = 1.1892 × 10⁻⁶ m²/s, ρ = 1025.9 kg/m³, pv = 1705 Pa). The coefficients depend only on Re, so the same network serves any chord and speed. The section cavitates when σ < σi; the safe angle is the lower of stall onset and cavitation inception.

Uncertainty (±). Each result carries the numerical uncertainty of the CFD it was trained on (grid study with the factor-of-safety method of Xing and Stern, combined with the iterative error of the stop rule; at Re 2.49 million for Re ≥ 1.3 million and at 0.8 million below) and the error of the surrogate (mean leave-one-Reynolds-number-out error, or twice the spread of the five networks if larger), added as root-sum-square. Drag carries the largest uncertainty (25–51 % from 6°), so use it for trends, not absolute values. Stall onset: ± 0.34° (surrogate 0.28°, solution path 0.2°); the OpenFOAM–Fluent difference is listed separately. A verdict is marked borderline when the margin is smaller than its uncertainty. Beyond stall onset the uncertainty is not quantified.

Flow pictures. The default animation is an illustration: ideal (potential) flow from the Joukowski mapping with the Kutta condition, circulation matched to the surrogate CL, pressure colours scaled to the predicted Cp,min, separation drawn from the lift loss, and bubbles drawn as a symbol when σ < σi. The OpenFOAM field view shows the nearest of 29 computed steady RANS fields (7 Reynolds numbers 1.39–8.0 million at α = 0°, 6°, 10°, 14°, plus 9.6° at 2.49 million): pressure or speed, streaks moving with the computed velocity, and in magenta the cells whose pressure is below vapour pressure at the chosen σ. RANS is single-phase, so neither view simulates cavities; the magenta region marks cavitation inception.

Pressure distribution. Stage 3: the pressure coefficient on 2 × 120 points along the chord is predicted by a reduced-order model (10 POD modes) driven by a mean of five neural networks (2 × 24 tanh) whose inputs are α, log Re and the stage-1 CL and σi. It was trained on 133 OpenFOAM pressure curves (Re 1.39–8.0 million, α −4° to 14°). Leaving out each interior Reynolds number in turn, the predicted curves differ from the CFD by 0.018 in Cp (rms) and Cp,min by 1.4 % on average (5.0 % at most); leaving out angles, 2.0 % on average (7.9 % at most). The shaded band combines that error with twice the spread of the five networks. Cavitation starts where Cp is lowest; the stretch marked in red is where Cp < −σ at the chosen depth. Beside the prediction, the tool draws our own OpenFOAM pressure curves at the Reynolds numbers nearest to the one entered (the run below and the run above, or the single run if it matches), at the nearest computed angle; these are the raw CFD results, not interpolated.

Same model and results as the thesis design tool (predict.py), checked case by case. Two-dimensional, steady, fully turbulent RANS; use 0.5° below the safe angle as a design margin. Md. Ziaul Karim and K.M. Rezabuzzaman Utso, NAME 400 thesis, BUET (supervisor Dr. Mir Tareque Ali).
